66050-dirty-work-for-doughgod.title: Dirty Work For Doughgod
66050-dirty-work-for-doughgod.creator: W. C. Tuttle
66050-dirty-work-for-doughgod.description: A book by W. C. Tuttle. “Now, now, Chuck,” says Doughgod, setting down with us. It’s two against one, and I’m the one. Also, I’m sort of up against it. I didn’t know them snake-huntin’ cohorts of mine were so bitter against women—honest to gosh! That Miss—” Doughgod scratched his head—“I don’t know her name right now—well, she sounds on paper like a regular teacher; so I told her to come and take the job.

arxiv-2105-14157.title: SMURF: Efficient and Scalable Metadata Access for Distributed Applications
arxiv-2105-14157.creator: Bing Zhang, Tevfik Kosar
arxiv-2105-14157.description: Abstract In parallel with big data processing and analysis dominating the usage of distributed and cloud infrastructures, the demand for distributed metadata access and transfer has increased. In many application domains, the volume of data generated exceeds petabytes, while the corresponding metadata amounts to terabytes or even more.

arxiv-2111-14161.title: Characterization measurements of the TRISTAN multi-pixel silicon drift detector
arxiv-2111-14161.creator: J. Wolf
arxiv-2111-14161.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. Wolf. Sterile neutrinos are a minimal extension of the Standard Model of Particle Physics. A laboratory-based approach to search for this particle is via tritium β-decay, where a sterile neutrino would cause a kink-like spectral distortion. The Karlsruhe Tritium Neutrino (KATRIN) experiment extended by a multi-pixel Silicon Drift Detector system has the potential to reach an unprecedented sensitivity to the keV-scale sterile neutrino in a lab-based experiment. The new detector system combines good spectroscopic performance with a high rate capability.

arxiv-2209-07675.title: An exact category approach to Hecke endomorphism algebras ∗
arxiv-2209-07675.creator: Jie Du, Brian Parshall †, Leonard Scott
arxiv-2209-07675.description: Abstract . Let G G be a finite group of Lie type. In studying the cross-characteristic representation theory of G G , the (specialized) Hecke algebra H = End G ​ ( Ind B G ​ 1 B ) H=\text{\rm{End}}_{G}(\text{Ind}_{B}^{G}1_{B}) has played a important role.

arxiv-2306-04607.title: GeoDiffusion: Text-Prompted Geometric Control for Object Detection Data Generation
arxiv-2306-04607.creator: Kai Chen, Enze Xie, Zhe Chen, Yibo Wang, Lanqing Hong, Zhenguo Li , Dit-Yan Yeung
arxiv-2306-04607.description: Abstract Diffusion models have attracted significant attention due to the remarkable ability to create content and generate data for tasks like image classification. However, the usage of diffusion models to generate the high-quality object detection data remains an underexplored area, where not only image-level perceptual quality but also geometric conditions such as bounding boxes and camera views are essential.

arxiv-2307-03690.title: Suppressing unknown disturbances to dynamical systems using machine learning
arxiv-2307-03690.creator: Juan G. Restrepo, Clayton P. Byers, Per Sebastian Skardal
arxiv-2307-03690.description: Abstract Identifying and suppressing unknown disturbances to dynamical systems is a problem with applications in many different fields. Here we present a model-free method to identify and suppress an unknown disturbance to an unknown system based only on previous observations of the system under the influence of a known forcing function.

arxiv-2405-20498.title: Robust Decentralized Control of Coupled Systems via Risk Sensitive Control of Decoupled or Simple Models with Measure Change
arxiv-2405-20498.creator: Zachary Selk, Serdar Yüksel
arxiv-2405-20498.description: Abstract Decentralized stochastic control problems with local information involve problems where multiple agents and subsystems which are coupled via dynamics and/or cost are present. Typically, however, the dynamics of such couplings is complex and difficult to precisely model, leading to questions on robustness in control design.

arxiv-2411-00604.title: ConvCounsel: A Conversational Dataset for Student Counseling
arxiv-2411-00604.creator: Po-Chuan Chen, Mahdin Rohmatillah, You-Teng Lin, Jen-Tzung Chien
arxiv-2411-00604.description: Abstract Student mental health is a sensitive issue that necessitates special attention. A primary concern is the student-to-counselor ratio, which surpasses the recommended standard of 250:1 in most universities. This imbalance results in extended waiting periods for in-person consultations, which cause suboptimal treatment.

arxiv-2501-18416.title: Exploring Potential Prompt Injection Attacks in Federated Military LLMs and Their Mitigation
arxiv-2501-18416.creator: Youngjoon Lee, Taehyun Park, Yunho Lee, Jinu Gong, Joonhyuk Kang
arxiv-2501-18416.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) is increasingly being adopted in military collaborations to develop Large Language Models (LLMs) while preserving data sovereignty. However, prompt injection attacks—malicious manipulations of input prompts—pose new threats that may undermine operational security, disrupt decision-making, and erode trust among allies.

arxiv-2505-09339.title: RAG-Enabled Intent Reasoning for Application-Network Interaction Thanks: Mohammed S. Elbamby contributed to this work as a member of Nokia Bell Labs Finland until February 2024.
arxiv-2505-09339.creator: Salwa Mostafa, Mohamed K. Abdel-Aziz, Mohammed S. Elbamby, Mehdi Bennis
arxiv-2505-09339.description: Abstract Intent-based network (IBN) is a promising solution to automate network operation and management. IBN aims to offer human-tailored network interaction, allowing the network to communicate in a way that aligns with the network users’ language, rather than requiring the network users to understand the technical language of the network/devices.

arxiv-2505-16357.title: Efficient Probabilistic Model Checking for Relational Reachability
arxiv-2505-16357.creator: Lina Gerlach, Tobias Winkler, Erika Ábrahám, Borzoo Bonakdarpour, Sebastian Junges
arxiv-2505-16357.description: Abstract Markov decision processes model systems subject to nondeterministic and probabilistic uncertainty. A plethora of verification techniques addresses variations of reachability properties, such as: Is there a scheduler resolving the nondeterminism such that the probability to reach an error state is above a threshold?

arxiv-2511-06441.title: Towards Resource-Efficient Multimodal Intelligence: Learned Routing among Specialized Expert Models
arxiv-2511-06441.creator: Mayank Saini, Arit Kumar Bishwas
arxiv-2511-06441.description: Abstract As AI moves beyond text, large language models (LLMs) increasingly power vision, audio, and document understanding; however, their high inference costs hinder real-time, scalable deployment. Conversely, smaller open-source models offer cost advantages but struggle with complex or multimodal queries.

arxiv-2602-17952.title: Hardware-Friendly Input Expansion for Accelerating Function Approximation
arxiv-2602-17952.creator: Hu Lou, Yin-Jun Gao*, Dong-Xiao Zhang*, Tai-Jiao Du, Jun-Jie Zhang, Jia-Rui Zhang
arxiv-2602-17952.description: Abstract One-dimensional function approximation is a fundamental problem in scientific computing and engineering applications. While neural networks possess powerful universal approximation capabilities, their optimization process is often hindered by flat loss landscapes induced by parameter-space symmetries, leading to slow convergence and poor generalization, particularly for high-frequency components.

britannica-1911-sunstone.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-sunstone.description: Article 'Sunstone' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 26), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. spangled appearance, which has led to its use as an ornamental stone. The effect appears to be due to reflections from enclosures of red haematite, in the form of minute scales, which are hexagonal, rhombic or irregular in shape, and are disposed parallel to the principal cleavage-plane.

doe-osti-3002319-modular-hydronic-room-c.title: Modular Hydronic Room Conditioning System
doe-osti-3002319-modular-hydronic-room-c.creator: Nawaz, Kashif, Gao, Lei, Bae, Yeonjin et al.
doe-osti-3002319-modular-hydronic-room-c.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. doe-osti-3015389-informing-transmission-.title: Informing Transmission Supply Chain Needs from National Transmission Studies
doe-osti-3015389-informing-transmission-.creator: Rose, Amy, Fuchs, Becca, Ramirez, Lina et al.
doe-osti-3015389-informing-transmission-.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. Recent national studies indicate significant transmission expansion can provide the lowest-cost option to maintain grid reliability while meeting growing demand. However, constraints in domestic supply chains may limit grid expansion across the U.S., with higher costs and longer

plos-pone-0001036.title: A Simple Method for Combining Genetic Mapping Data from Multiple Crosses and Experimental Designs
plos-pone-0001036.creator: Jeremy L. Peirce, Karl W. Broman, Lu Lu et al.
plos-pone-0001036.description: PLOS ONE research article. Over the past decade many linkage studies have defined chromosomal intervals containing polymorphisms that modulate a variety of traits. Many phenotypes are now associated with enough mapping data that meta-analysis could help refine locations of known QTLs and detect many novel

pmc-10709600.title: Inner core static tilt inferred from intradecadal oscillation in the Earth’s rotation
pmc-10709600.creator: Yachong An, Hao Ding, Zhifeng Chen, Wenbin Shen, Weiping Jiang
pmc-10709600.description: The presence of a static tilt between the inner core and mantle is an ongoing discussion encompassing the geodynamic state of the inner core. Here, we confirm an approximate 8.5 yr signal in polar motion is the inner core wobble (ICW), and find that the ICW is also contained in the length-of-day variations of the Earth’s rotation.

pmc-11432691.title: Mark–Release–Recapture Trial with Aedes albopictus (Diptera, Culicidae) Irradiated Males: Population Parameters and Climatic Factors
pmc-11432691.creator: Fátima Isabel Falcão Amaro, Patricia Soares, Enkelejda Velo, Danilo Oliveira Carvalho, Maylen Gomez, Fabrizio Balestrino, Arianna Puggioli, Romeo Bellini, Hugo Costa Osório
pmc-11432691.description: Simple SummaryAedes albopictus mosquitoes spread arboviruses like dengue, Zika, or chikungunya. The Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) can be used as a prevention and control tool against Ae. albopictus populations. Mark–release–recapture (MRR) trials are fundamental to estimate the size of the wild population in target areas and to determine the dispersal capacity and survival of sterile males in open field conditions.

pmc-11600047.title: First measurement report for volatile organic compounds characteristics during winter in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
pmc-11600047.creator: Soo Ran Won, Yong Pyo Kim, Misheel Sainjargal, Tseren-Ochir Soyol-Erdene, Ji Yi Lee
pmc-11600047.description: In this study, 34 volatile organic compounds (VOCs) were analyzed using an online VOCs instrument at 30-min intervals from November 16 to November 23, 2023, in Ulaanbaatar (UB), the capital of Mongolia for the first time. The average concentration of the 34 VOCs was 13.0 ± 11.

pmc-11656721.title: Ngā Māuiui Kai: creating Indigenous Māori terms for eating disorders in Aotearoa New Zealand
pmc-11656721.creator: Gloria Fraser, Mau Te Rangimarie Clark, Bailey Mary Rose, Kacey Martin, Brittani Beavis, Michaela Pettie, Jennifer Jordan, Keri Opai
pmc-11656721.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMāori (the Indigenous people of Aotearoa New Zealand) report higher rates of eating disorders than non-Māori, but access treatment at lower rates. Diagnostic terms lacking in cultural relevance likely contribute to Māori exclusion in eating disorder spaces.

pmc-11690983.title: LIFETIME PATTERNS OF EXPOSURE TO JOB COMPLEXITY AND LATER LIFE COGNITION
pmc-11690983.creator: Qize Chen, Joanne Hsu, Yun taek Oh, Jacqui Smith, Amanda Sonnega
pmc-11690983.description: A growing body of evidence establishes a positive connection between cognitively engaging activities and later life cognitive functioning. Cognitively stimulating work—jobs that involve complex tasks and demands—is gaining increased research attention in this regard. Given data limitations to date, however, less research has focused on exposure to job complexity over the entire adult life course.

pmc-12565264.title: Modelling the Effect of Viruses on Insect Survival: Using a Second-Order Phase Transition Model to Describe Time–Effect and Dose–Effect Relationships Using Entomopathogenic Viruses as an Example
pmc-12565264.creator: Vladislav Soukhovolsky, Anton Kovalev, Olga Tarasova, Dmitry Kurenshchikov, Yuriy Tokarev, Daria Kharlamova, Yuriy Akhanaev, Sergey Pavlushin, Vyacheslav Martemyanov
pmc-12565264.description: Simple SummaryThis study explores how viruses can control forest insects by examining how the amount of virus and exposure time affect insect death rates. The goal was to create simple mathematical models to predict how well viruses work against insect pests.

pmc-12854339.title: Knowledge of undergraduate nursing students about palliative care
pmc-12854339.creator: Aruna Jothishanmugam
pmc-12854339.description: BACKGROUND:Palliative care is an essential component of holistic health care that aims to improve the quality of life for patients with life-threatening illnesses. Nurses play a crucial role in delivering palliative care, yet knowledge gaps persist, particularly among nursing students. This study assesses nursing students’ knowledge of palliative care and identifies areas for improvement to enhance nursing education.

pmc-13183463.title: Real-world experience with rituximab for multiple sclerosis treatment in a Brazilian tertiary center
pmc-13183463.creator: Ana Beatriz Simon-Nogueira, Arthur Cesário de Holanda, Rafael Augusto Rosalem, Thiago Ivan Vilchez Santillan, Guilherme Diogo Silva, Samira Luisa Apostolos-Pereira, Tarso Adoni, Dagoberto Callegaro, Mariana Gondim Spricigo, Mateus Boaventura de Oliveira
pmc-13183463.description: BackgroundRituximab, an anti-cluster of differentiation 20 (anti-CD20) monoclonal antibody, has been widely used off-label for multiple sclerosis (MS) treatment, demonstrating high effectiveness and a favorable safety profile. However, real-world data from Brazil, particularly within the public healthcare system, remain scarce.ObjectiveTo assess the real-world effectiveness and safety of rituximab for MS treatment in a Brazilian tertiary center.

pmc-13209284.title: Circadian Modulation of Protein Catabolism: Insight from a Population Study
pmc-13209284.creator: Miriam Lisa Kafader, Sébastien Sare, Martina Zandonà, Rosaria Del Giorno, Maria Luisa Garo, Sandro Bonetti, Luca Gabutti
pmc-13209284.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Urinary urea excretion is a marker of protein catabolism and follows circadian biological rhythms. Although small-scale studies have suggested a diurnal pattern, its population-level characterisation and determinants remain poorly defined. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted within the Ticino Epidemiological Stiffness Study (TEST-study), a population-based cross-sectional analysis of 1202 adults (≥18 years) recruited in the Italian-speaking region of Switzerland in 2017–2018.

pmc-13217470.title: Relationship typologies with online sexual partners and condomless anal intercourse among men who have sex with men: Evidence from latent class analysis and multilevel regression
pmc-13217470.creator: Luyao Xie, Angela Yuen Chun Li, Alex Siu Wing Chan, Ho Hin Lee, Meiqi Xin, Zixin Wang, Joseph Tak Fai Lau, Phoenix Kit Han Mo
pmc-13217470.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). pmc-13507184.title: Scalable phase-change fibres with record thermo-mechanical properties for cooling textiles
pmc-13507184.creator: Xiaolong Li, Qianyi Li, Xiaoyu Zhang, Tural Khudiyev

pmc-13582507.title: The “puberty deadline”: cultural constructions of maturity, anticipated shame, and child marriage as a perceived risk-mitigation strategy in rural Niger
pmc-13582507.creator: Jean Christophe Fotso, Aichatou Hamadou, Ferdinard Ngong, Paul Bukuluki
pmc-13582507.description: IntroductionIn rural Niger, child marriage remains highly prevalent, often functioning as a mechanism of risk mitigation. This qualitative study explores the cultural and bio-social drivers of child marriage, focusing on the intersection of physical maturation, anticipatory shame, and economic vulnerability.
